investigation.deliverable: Cited explanation or recommendation; read-only investigation.

steps.action: State the question and interpretation when ambiguous; inspect existing context before asking.
steps.failure: Missing facts stay explicit unknowns; do not silently turn investigation into a fix.

steps.action: Trace entry points, runtime flow, structures and boundaries. Simple scope takes one pass; complex scope uses 2–4 distinct read-only exploration angles and a synthesis.
steps.failure: Name any untraced boundary and conflicting findings.

steps.action: For motivation, anchor files/lines/symbols/history, search each available evidence category, preserve direct/supported/inferred/speculative/unknown confidence.
steps.failure: Unavailable connectors and empty searches remain distinct gaps; code behavior does not prove intent.

steps.action: Present cited Overview, Key Concepts, How It Works, Where Things Live, Gotchas as applicable; alternatives get tradeoffs and an actual judgment.
steps.failure: Do not invent citations or make code changes. Re-route only when repair is authorized.

bug-fix.deliverable: Minimal evidence-supported repair and original-surface failing-to-passing reproduction.

steps.action: Reproduce via the actual affected UI/CLI/API under the relevant role/environment; link FEAT/AC/CHG and preserve raw failing output.
steps.failure: Tighten or synthesize trigger and instrument until reproduced. Ask user only after driving as far as reachable and naming the specific unreachable surface.

steps.action: Use how and why to seed alternatives; choose the next observation that removes the most uncertainty; collect runtime observations before eliminating each hypothesis.
steps.failure: Stubborn failures require a changed hypothesis and new evidence, not blind retries.

steps.action: Confirm the surviving mechanism with runtime evidence before implementation or design review; inspect sibling patterns and persisted config/cache/locks after restart.
steps.failure: No speculative guards or guessed fixes may be called confirmed.

steps.action: When evidence refutes a hypothesis, revert only trial edits it motivated and preserve unrelated user changes.
steps.failure: Record the scoped revert and resulting state; never reset the whole dirty workspace.

steps.action: For cross-function changes, compare at least two grounded designs using applicable architect guidance. Delegate bounded implementation where useful and review the diff.
steps.failure: Do not retain a design when repeated implementation friction disproves it.

steps.action: For a cheap clear test, capture intended failing-before behavior before fixing; then capture passing-after and nearby regression. Deliver coherent ordered units.
steps.failure: For expensive/integration-heavy/unclear tests, explain the reason before fixing and use the closest executable reproduction, never weaken intended assertions.

steps.action: Replay the original user path with the same surface, environment and role; observe the intended result and relevant persisted state after restart.
steps.failure: Wrong surface, inconclusive output, unit checks alone or toast alone cannot establish bug absence.

steps.action: Report what broke, root cause, minimal fix, and exact failing/passing output. Follow project delivery rules with a reviewed diff and retained evidence.
steps.failure: Unverified branches remain gaps; a review-ready protocol is not an executed repair.

runtime-forensics.deliverable: Diagnosis from new live instrumentation; no product fix unless separately authorized.

steps.action: Capture a real CPU profile for spin, heap snapshot for leak or UI/CDP trace for visual glitch from the matching live surface.
steps.failure: Record precise missing capture tool, permission or process; plain logs cannot stand in for all profiler types.

steps.action: Reduce to hot function, retained-object to GC-root chain or unexpected input-free loop; large artifacts use bounded parsing delegates.
steps.failure: Retain the raw artifact and exact reduction query; do not infer the runtime cause only from source.

steps.action: Prove the mechanism with appropriate reversible live instrumentation or an authorized ephemeral live intervention.
steps.failure: Unavailable confirmation limits confidence; do not modify persisted product code merely to produce a diagnosis.

steps.action: Map the finding to source file, symbol and allocator/scheduler line using runtime observations.
steps.failure: Unresolved symbols remain an explicit attribution gap.

steps.action: Return signal, reduced finding, mechanism proof, source location and raw artifact paths; route to repair or performance work only when requested.
steps.failure: Do not claim shipped fixes from a diagnostic run.

trace-forensics.deliverable: Diagnosis from a supplied immutable captured artifact; no automatic live recapture.

steps.action: Identify cpuprofile, JSON/gzip trace, spindump or heap format and use an appropriate parser; preserve original bytes.
steps.failure: Malformed or unsupported artifact remains a precise gap, not permission to silently recapture.

steps.action: Transform into queryable samples/frames/nodes (for example SQLite) before analysis and retain transformations and queries.
steps.failure: A narrative summary without a traceable queryable representation is incomplete.

steps.action: Query time-heavy frames and call tree; leaks follow retainers to GC roots; spindumps identify CPU/blocked thread and wait reason.
steps.failure: No supporting data means no confirmed hot path or retainer claim.

steps.action: Map hot frames using artifact symbols to file, symbol and line; resolve available symbol bundles.
steps.failure: State plainly when the artifact lacks mapping and cannot support attributed diagnosis.

steps.action: When a comparable paired capture exists, compare before/after artifacts.
steps.failure: Without a pair, use bounded strongest-supported-hypothesis language; never claim confirmed improvement.

steps.action: Return artifact format, finding, source mapping, artifact paths and paired-confirmation status. Fix only on subsequent authorization.
steps.failure: A supplied trace is a fixed dataset; do not pretend it is a new live observation.

perf-issue.operation: Measure the reported path with the project's existing profiler, change one supported cause, and compare on the same path.
perf-issue.prerequisite: A measured baseline and an operable project surface.
perf-issue.limit: No pstack performance playbook is installed; a diagnosis is not an improvement.

hillclimb.operation: Fix a metric and target, run bounded before/after experiments with the project's checks, and retain accepted results.
hillclimb.prerequisite: An agreed metric, repeatable baseline, and bounded experiment budget.
hillclimb.limit: No pstack hillclimb loop is installed; stop when cost or evidence bounds are reached.

feature.capability: codex-engineering feature map and project checks
feature.operation: Read the project's requirement and map, implement the named behavior, then verify its user entry point and update the map.
feature.prerequisite: An authorized feature and a bound project.
feature.limit: The route does not authorize a new product scope or claim the feature was built.

refactoring.operation: Capture behavior at affected entry points, make the smallest structure change, and replay the same checks.
refactoring.prerequisite: An identified code boundary and applicable regression path.
refactoring.limit: No behavior change is implied by this route.

prototype.operation: Build a disposable variant for the specific decision and observe the deciding behavior.
prototype.prerequisite: A stated decision and isolated data or workspace.
prototype.limit: A prototype is not a shipped feature.

visual-parity.capability: existing browser control and image comparison
visual-parity.operation: Open both matching UI states, capture comparable views, inspect differences, and verify the corrected interaction.
visual-parity.prerequisite: Both target views and matching viewport, role, and data.
visual-parity.limit: A screenshot alone does not prove business behavior.

authoring-a-skill.operation: Read the local skill-creator instructions, edit the requested skill, validate its structure, and try its entry point.
authoring-a-skill.prerequisite: A named skill and writable skill source.
authoring-a-skill.limit: Do not present pstack's authoring playbook as adopted.

eval.operation: Define held-out examples and an acceptance rule, run the existing harness, and inspect its false positives and failures.
eval.prerequisite: An available evaluation harness and non-leaking held-out cases.
eval.limit: A judge score does not replace actual project behavior.

babysit.operation: Inspect the actual PR, checks, conflicts, and review comments; address concrete blockers and rerun affected checks.
babysit.prerequisite: An accessible existing PR and authorized repository access.
babysit.limit: No PR is created or merged by classification alone.

shipping.operation: Review the exact release candidate, verify its gates and rollback, then use the project's authorized release path.
shipping.prerequisite: A concrete candidate, release instructions, and required authorization.
shipping.limit: Green tests alone do not authorize a merge or deployment.

autonomous-run.capability: current Codex task and project controls
autonomous-run.operation: Continue the bounded authorized task to its completion predicate, recording blockers and tested results.
autonomous-run.prerequisite: A concrete completion predicate and current task context.
autonomous-run.limit: It does not create an unattended pstack execution loop.

orchestrate.operation: Split independent project work into owned scopes, coordinate shared state, and integrate verified outputs.
orchestrate.prerequisite: An explicitly delegated multi-part project and independent work scopes.
orchestrate.limit: No standing pstack coordinator or automatic multi-day supervision is installed.

autopilot-full.capability: manual Codex task and repository workflow
autopilot-full.operation: Handle each authorized PR as a separately verified task and use repository tools for any approved integration.
autopilot-full.prerequisite: A real PR queue, repository access, and integration authorization.
autopilot-full.limit: No automatic queue-to-merge service is installed.

autopilot-stack.capability: manual Git worktree and review workflow
autopilot-stack.operation: Build and verify a requested ordered stack in isolated branches, retaining dependency and review evidence.
autopilot-stack.prerequisite: A real branch stack, repository access, and an agreed base.
autopilot-stack.limit: No automatic stack builder or landing service is installed.

session-pickup.operation: Read the latest handoff, inspect the actual workspace and evidence, then resume only the unfinished work.
session-pickup.prerequisite: A prior task or handoff reference.
session-pickup.limit: Old status text does not override current workspace facts.

pause-safely.operation: Record current state, unfinished action, running process and evidence locations before stopping.
pause-safely.prerequisite: An explicit pause or imminent session interruption.
pause-safely.limit: Do not mark unfinished work complete.

multi-phase-plan.capability: current project plan and dependency checks
multi-phase-plan.operation: Sequence deliverables by dependency, name evidence gates, and implement each authorized phase.
multi-phase-plan.prerequisite: A task spanning distinct phases or dependent changes.
multi-phase-plan.limit: A plan is not execution or acceptance.

worktree-cleanup.operation: List worktrees, check branch and uncommitted state, and remove only explicitly safe targets through Git.
worktree-cleanup.prerequisite: A Git repository and an identified cleanup target.
worktree-cleanup.limit: Never infer an unmerged or dirty worktree is disposable.

opening-a-pr.operation: Verify the diff and checks, create the requested PR against the actual repository, and attach its link.
opening-a-pr.prerequisite: A Git repository, remote, reviewed diff, and PR authorization.
opening-a-pr.limit: A route result does not create a PR or imply a review verdict.

figure-it-out.capability: current Codex planning and project controls
figure-it-out.operation: For a large cross-cutting or genuinely unmatched task, ground the affected systems, define the bounded deliverable and evidence gates, then choose an applicable execution route.
figure-it-out.prerequisite: A concrete large task or a checked absence of matching playbooks.
figure-it-out.limit: This is a local preparatory route, not an adopted pstack figure-it-out execution workflow or permission to reopen an already approved plan.
